arguments.command:
python3 << 'EOF'
import numpy as np

# Foreign and international holdings at end of March for years 2000-2004 (in billions USD)
holdings = [1085.0, 1012.5, 1057.2, 1275.2, 1670.0]

# Calculate annual returns (percentage change)
returns = []
for i in range(1, len(holdings)):
    ret = (holdings[i] - holdings[i-1]) / holdings[i-1]
    returns.append(ret)
    print(f"Year {2000+i}: Return = {ret*100:.4f}%")

# Convert to numeric array
returns = np.array(returns)
print(f"\nReturns: {returns}")

# Mean and std
mean_ret = np.mean(returns)
std_ret = np.std(returns, ddof=1)  # Sample std
print(f"Mean return: {mean_ret*100:.4f}%")
print(f"Std dev: {std_ret*100:.4f}%")

# For 1% lower-tail with small sample, use mean - 2.33*std (approximate z-score for 1%)
# This is a parametric approach
var_1pct = mean_ret - 2.33 * std_ret
print(f"\n1% VaR (as return): {var_1pct*100:.4f}%")

# The question asks about the loss on the holdings at end of March 2004
# So we apply this return to the 2004 holdings
portfolio_2004 = holdings[-1]  # 1670.0 billion USD
usd_loss = portfolio_2004 * var_1pct
print(f"\nPortfolio value (2004): ${portfolio_2004} billion")
print(f"1% VaR (USD): ${usd_loss} billion")

# Convert to JPY using March 2004 exchange rate (March 1, 2004)
# USD -> JPY exchange rate = 108.5157
exchange_rate = 108.5157
jpy_loss = usd_loss * exchange_rate
print(f"\nExchange rate (March 1, 2004): {exchange_rate}")
print(f"1% VaR (JPY): {jpy_loss} billion")
print(f"Rounded: {round(jpy_loss)} billion")
EOF

# Re-verify the calculation
# Foreign and international holdings at end of March for years 2000-2004 (in billions USD)
holdings = [1085.0, 1012.5, 1057.2, 1275.2, 1670.0]

# Calculate annual returns (percentage change)
returns = []
for i in range(1, len(holdings)):
    ret = (holdings[i] - holdings[i-1]) / holdings[i-1]
    returns.append(ret)
    print(f"Return from {2000+i-1} to {2000+i}: {ret*100:.4f}%")

# Mean and std with sample standard deviation (ddof=1)
n = len(returns)
mean_ret = sum(returns) / n

# Sample variance and std (using n-1 denominator)
variance = sum((r - mean_ret) ** 2 for r in returns) / (n - 1)
std_ret = variance ** 0.5

print(f"\nMean return: {mean_ret*100:.4f}%")
print(f"Std dev: {std_ret*100:.4f}%")

# For 1% lower-tail (VaR at 99% confidence), use z-score of 2.33
# VaR = mean - z * std (for lower tail)
z_score = 2.33
var_1pct = mean_ret - z_score * std_ret
print(f"\n1% VaR (as return): {var_1pct*100:.4f}%")

# The portfolio at end of March 2004
portfolio_2004 = holdings[-1]  # 1670.0 billion USD

# Convert to loss (make positive for loss magnitude)
# VaR represents a loss when negative return
usd_loss = abs(portfolio_2004 * var_1pct)
print(f"\nPortfolio at end of March 2004: ${portfolio_2004} billion USD")
print(f"1% lower-tail VaR (USD): ${usd_loss:.2f} billion")

# Convert to JPY using March 1, 2004 exchange rate
exchange_rate = 108.5157
jpy_loss = usd_loss * exchange_rate
print(f"\nExchange rate (March 1, 2004): {exchange_rate} JPY/USD")
print(f"1% VaR (JPY): {jpy_loss:.2f} billion JPY")
print(f"\nRounded to nearest whole billion: {round(jpy_loss)} billion JPY")
EOF
